insights.title: Card charge-off guidance lowered to 3.2%
insights.summary: Management guided the 2026 card net charge-off rate to about 3.4% on the Q4 2025 call and kept that figure on the Q1 2026 call. On the Q2 2026 call it was lowered to about 3.2%, attributed to better-than-expected consumer credit performance.
insights.uw_relevance: Card loss expectations are a core credit driver for a large card book. The revised figure is management's own forward view and is a point to test against delinquency and charge-off data.

insights.title: Consumer deposit growth outlook narrowed over 2026
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call management said 2026 consumer deposit growth was lower than its scenario analysis. On the Q1 2026 call the expected range was low to mid-single digits. On the Q2 2026 call it was low single-digit, with yield-seeking flows described as a continuing factor and probably a risk.
insights.uw_relevance: Deposit growth and funding stability bear on liquidity and funding risk for a bank. The narrowing of the stated range over three calls is a change in management's own funding outlook.

insights.title: Private credit underwriting weakness acknowledged
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call management said it was quite mindful of risks in nonbank financial institution lending. On the Q1 2026 call the CEO cited some weakening in underwriting across the market, not just in private credit. On the Q2 2026 call he described weaker covenants and more rollover risk across some players, while saying the issue was not systemic.

insights.title: SEC supervisory failure censure
insights.summary: The SEC censured JPMorgan Chase and its securities unit for failing to supervise a disqualified person who traded without permission from late 2021 to early 2024; no fine, but a cease-and-desist order was issued.

followups.question: How is management managing the rise in uninsured deposits to 64.3% of total deposits, and how much of the uninsured balance sits in yield-seeking or concentrated corporate accounts?
followups.summary: Uninsured deposits reached 64.3% of total deposits in FY2026 Q2, up from 60.9% in FY2025 Q4, an estimated $1,743.90B. The average liquidity coverage ratio was 110.0% in FY2026 Q2, against 112.0% in FY2026 Q1.
followups.uw_relevance: A higher uninsured share increases the funding outflow a bank could face in stress, and the filing names loss of deposits as a liquidity risk.

followups.question: How has the approximately $50 billion private credit exposure performed since management described weaker covenants and more rollover risk, and how is it reflected in the allowance for loan losses?
followups.summary: Core non-bank financial institution exposure is about $160 billion, of which about $50 billion is private credit. On the Q2 2026 call the CEO described weaker covenants and more rollover risk across some players.
followups.uw_relevance: Management itself flags private credit expansion as a possible source of losses, so the answer bears directly on credit quality and reserve adequacy.

followups.question: What drove the cut in the 2026 card net charge-off guidance from about 3.4% to about 3.2%, and what delinquency data supports it given the higher gas prices and inflation management cited?
followups.summary: Management guided 2026 card net charge-offs to about 3.4% and lowered the figure to about 3.2% on the Q2 2026 call, attributing it to better-than-expected consumer credit performance. The same call cited elevated gas prices and inflation as pressures on consumers.
followups.uw_relevance: Card loss expectations are a core credit driver, and a lower forward estimate that is not backed by delinquency data would be a reporting risk.

followups.question: How much of the roughly $20 billion of added G-SIB capital is already reflected in the CET1 ratio, and how would a 5.2% G-SIB requirement affect the buyback pace?
followups.summary: Management plans for a 5.2% G-SIB requirement in 2028, up 70 basis points from 4.5%, implying about $20 billion of added G-SIB capital. The CET1 ratio was 13.9% (preliminary) in FY2026 Q3, against 14.2% in FY2026 Q2, and share repurchases were $6.79B in FY2026 Q2.
followups.uw_relevance: Higher required capital could limit repurchases, and the regulatory dispute over the proposals is still active, which adds uncertainty to the capital base.

followups.question: What is the status and expected scope of the civil suit filed by President Donald J. Trump that names JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. and its CEO, and has the company assessed any exposure from it?
followups.summary: A January 2026 civil suit by President Donald J. Trump, personally and through affiliated entities, was filed in Florida state court and names JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. and its CEO. The matter is listed as open.
followups.uw_relevance: A suit naming the bank and its CEO directly, still open in the filings reviewed, creates potential personal and entity exposure for officers and the company.

followups.question: How will the transition to Co-Presidents be managed, and who will take over the President and COO role when Daniel Pinto retires at the end of 2026?
followups.summary: Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh were named Co-Presidents on 25 June 2026, and Daniel Pinto, President and COO, will retire at the end of 2026. Marianne Lake, former CEO of CCB, is also retiring.
followups.uw_relevance: Several senior departures and role changes in a short period raise key-person and succession risk across both main lines of business.

followups.question: Why did director Todd Combs give notice of resignation effective 7 December 2025, and has the board filled the vacancy?
followups.summary: Director Todd Combs gave notice of resignation from the Board effective 7 December 2025. Daniel Pinto, President and COO, will retire at the end of 2026.
followups.uw_relevance: Board departures alongside senior executive changes affect continuity of oversight over risk, controls and capital decisions.

followups.question: What share of FY2026 Q2 fee income of $31.84B came from items management now expects will not repeat, and what fee level does management expect in coming quarters?
followups.summary: Fee income grew 46.7% year on year in FY2026 Q2, and management flags part of that quarter as pulled forward and unlikely to repeat. On the Q2 2026 call the CEO said the environment was close to as good as it gets.
followups.uw_relevance: Trading and deal-driven fees are volatile, so the non-repeating part of the quarter affects how the earnings base should be read.

followups.question: What is driving the rise in the FY2026 NII excluding Markets outlook to about $96.5B and the adjusted expense outlook to about $107.5B, and how much of the expense increase is tied to revenue-related costs?
followups.summary: On 14 July 2026 the firm raised its FY2026 NII excluding Markets outlook to about $96.5B from about $95B and its adjusted expense outlook to about $107.5B from about $105B, citing higher volume and revenue-related expense. Net interest margin was 2.4% in FY2026 Q2.
followups.uw_relevance: Higher expense guidance tied to revenue outperformance changes the operating plan and should be weighed against the revenue outlook.

followups.question: Which cyber breaches are described in the 10-K, what losses or regulatory consequences did they have, and what controls address the AI-related cyber risk management cited?
followups.summary: The 10-K states the firm has experienced security breaches from cyber attacks and that future breaches are inevitable. On the Q1 2026 call the CEO called cyber the firm's largest risk and said AI has made cyber risk worse and harder.
followups.uw_relevance: Management names cyber as its largest risk and the filing describes past breaches, making it a specific exposure for D&O review.

followups.question: What operational and credit integration plan covers the Apple Card portfolio during the roughly 24 months before closing, and what does the $2.2B in the provision line relate to?
followups.summary: Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card under a forward purchase commitment entered 30 December 2025, with closing expected about 24 months later. Filings footnote $2.2B associated with the transaction in the provision line.
followups.uw_relevance: A large consumer credit portfolio with a long closing period adds credit and operational exposure during integration.

followups.question: What drove the rise in average total VaR at 95% to $49M in FY2026 Q2, and how do the trading limits respond to the energy-price and geopolitical volatility management cited?
followups.summary: Average Total VaR (95%) was $49M in FY2026 Q2, against $37M in FY2026 Q1. On the Q2 2026 call management cited elevated gas prices and inflation, and tied Middle East developments to deal timing and higher energy prices.
followups.uw_relevance: Rising trading value-at-risk alongside named geopolitical and energy channels bears on market losses that could fall on earnings and capital.

followups.question: What supervisory controls were changed after the SEC censure for failing to supervise a statutorily disqualified person who traded in the US without permission from late 2021 to early 2024?
followups.summary: The SEC censured JPMorgan Chase and its securities unit for failing to supervise a statutorily disqualified person who traded in the US without permission from late 2021 to early 2024. The bank was not fined, and the SEC issued a cease-and-desist order.
followups.uw_relevance: A supervisory failure finding with a cease-and-desist order is a conduct and oversight matter, even though no monetary penalty was imposed.

metric_relevance.buyback_intensity: Buybacks to net income fell to 0.32x in FY2026 Q2 from 0.50x in FY2026 Q1, versus 0.55x in FY2025. R3 ties the lower payout to the dividend increase, and it sits alongside the falling CET1 ratio in K1.
metric_relevance.buybacks: Share repurchases fell to $6.79B in FY2026 Q2 from $8.32B in FY2026 Q1, after $31.59B in FY2025. R3 links the slowdown to a planned rise in the quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share, and Q6 asks how both will be funded if capital rules tighten.
metric_relevance.cet1_ratio: CET1 fell from 15.7% in FY2024 Q4 to 14.2% in FY2026 Q2 and a preliminary 13.9% in FY2026 Q3. K1 and R8 show management planning for a 5.2% G-SIB requirement in 2028, making this the main capital pressure point.
metric_relevance.deposit_growth_yoy: Deposit growth slowed to 5.9% YoY in FY2026 Q2 from 7.2% in FY2026 Q1. Management narrowed its 2026 consumer deposit growth outlook to low single digits, and B2 notes yield-seeking flows as a probable risk.
metric_relevance.deposits: Total deposits reached $2,713.70B in FY2026 Q2, up from $2,559.32B at FY2025 Q4. R6 estimates $1,743.90B of these are uninsured, so the size of the funding base depends on the stability of uninsured balances.
metric_relevance.equity: Stockholders' equity rose to $374.60B in FY2026 Q2 from $362.44B at FY2025 Q4. It is the base for ROE and the unrealized loss ratio, and K1 and R8 show that higher G-SIB requirements are measured against this capital base.
metric_relevance.fee_income_growth_yoy: Fee income grew 46.7% YoY in FY2026 Q2, following -20.9% in FY2025 Q2, which shows a cyclical swing. K7 notes that noninterest income reached 1.25x net interest income and that management expects the equities result to be hard to repeat.
metric_relevance.lcr: LCR fell to 110.0% in FY2026 Q2 from 112.0% in FY2026 Q1 and 113.0% in FY2025 Q2. K2 and R6 link this decline to rising uninsured deposits, which raises the question of funding stability under stress.
metric_relevance.loan_loss_reserve_ratio: The allowance to loans ratio was 1.8% in FY2026 Q2, down from 1.9% through FY2024 Q4 to FY2025 Q3. K8 sets this against nonperforming loans rising to 0.7% and lower card charge-off guidance, which Q3 asks management to explain.
metric_relevance.net_income: Net income was $21.16B in FY2026 Q2 and $15.30B in FY2026 Q3, while FY2025 totaled $57.05B against $58.47B in FY2024. Earnings are strong, but the FY2026 Q2 peak depends on the fee surge that K7 says may be partly pulled forward.
metric_relevance.nim: Net interest margin was 2.4% in FY2026 Q2 and 2.5% in FY2026 Q1, down from 2.7% in FY2023. R11 shows management raising its NII outlook on higher volume, so margin pressure may be offset by balance growth.
metric_relevance.noninterest_income: Noninterest income reached $31.84B in FY2026 Q2 from $24.47B in FY2026 Q1, against $87.00B for FY2025. K7 says the fee level is partly pulled forward, and B3 records management saying the environment was close to as good as it gets.
metric_relevance.npl_ratio: The nonperforming loan ratio rose to 0.7% at FY2025 Q4 from 0.5% at FY2023 Q4. K8 pairs this with lowered card net charge-off guidance of about 3.2%, and Q3 asks what supports that lower figure.
metric_relevance.revenue: Revenue was $57.35B in FY2026 Q2 and $50.17B in FY2026 Q3, against $45.80B in FY2025 Q4, so the top line is elevated. K7 flags the fee surge as partly pulled forward, so the current level may be hard to sustain.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_qoq: QoQ growth jumped to 15.1% in FY2026 Q2 after 8.8% in FY2026 Q1 and -1.4% in FY2025 Q4. B3 records management shifting to a cautious view after strong investment banking fees, so this spike may not persist.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_yoy: YoY growth of 27.7% in FY2026 Q2 follows -10.5% in FY2025 Q2, so the reported rate is distorted by a weak base. K7 says the equities result would be hard to repeat, which makes the spike a weak guide to trend.
metric_relevance.roa: ROA was 1.4% in FY2025, down from 1.5% in FY2024 and in line with 1.4% in FY2021. K10 presents profitability as sustained, but the figure does not show how much of the FY2026 quarterly earnings is tied to the fee surge.
metric_relevance.roe: ROE was 16.1% in FY2025 against 17.4% in FY2024, and K10 describes returns as sustained. Because ROE uses average equity, it is sensitive to equity growth as capital requirements rise.
metric_relevance.tier1_ratio: Tier 1 capital ratio declined from 16.8% in FY2024 Q4 to 15.1% in FY2026 Q2, on the same downward path as CET1. The fall is tied to the G-SIB and Basel III changes that R8 describes.
metric_relevance.uninsured_deposit_share: Uninsured deposits reached 64.3% of total deposits in FY2026 Q2, up from 60.9% at FY2025 Q4 and 56.1% at FY2023 Q4. K2 flags this alongside the weaker LCR, and Q2 asks how concentrated these balances are in the largest accounts.
metric_relevance.unrealized_loss_to_equity: Unrealized securities losses equal 4.9% of equity in FY2026 Q2, down from 7.8% at FY2024 Q4 and 12.6% at FY2022. It sits alongside the CET1 decline in K1 as a measure of balance-sheet capital strength.
